name: cdk-clipboard
description: Uses the cdkCopyToClipboard directive to copy text to the system clipboard on a button click, reacting to the (cdkCopyToClipboardCopied) event to confirm success.
notes: (cdkCopyToClipboardCopied) emits a boolean, not the copied text — it reports whether the underlying `document.execCommand('copy')` call succeeded, since some browsers can refuse it (e.g. without a recent user gesture).
cdkCopyToClipboard reads its bound value at click time, so binding it to a value that changes between renders is safe — there's no separate 'set clipboard content' step that could go stale.

Copying very large strings can fail silently on some browsers; for large payloads, check the emitted boolean and fall back to the async navigator.clipboard.writeText() API rather than assuming success.
